title: Lifeline pipe for the native lore binary, and the plugin installer's detached children (DEC-282 (a2) items 2 and 4)
description:
DEC-282 (a2) items 2 and 4, relayed by the leader 2026-11-19 from opum-doc origin/dev planning.json (DEC-282 outcome, opum-ai/opum-doc#1808, ODOC-634). Follows LCLI-797 (#734), which ships the wrapper's process-group shape and death-by-signal.
ITEM 2, lifeline: the wrapper holds the write end of a pipe that it passes to the native child. When the child reads EOF on it (the wrapper died by any signal including SIGKILL, or the caller killed the caller's group), the child kills its own group and exits. A pipe, not getppid()==1: portable and immediate, and macOS has no PDEATHSIG. Proof both ways: kill -9 on the wrapper, and kill -9 on the caller's group, each leaves no surviving native or grandchild process, plus a normal run unaffected. Needs a change in the native binary as well as bin/lore.cjs, so it is a DEC-182 (1) launcher-class build: sonnet or higher, opus security review, no DeepSeek.
ITEM 4: src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts:106 spawns detached children that escape either group design. Either stop detaching them, or track and kill them on shutdown and on lifeline EOF.
If this is not landed by the 0.15.0 pair cut, CHANGELOG.md states the residual (it already names both) and it ships in the next patch release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: kill -9 on the wrapper leaves no surviving native or grandchild process
kill -9 on the caller process group leaves no surviving native or grandchild process
a normal run is unaffected (argv, stdio, exit status)
agent-plugins.ts:106 detached children are no longer left running when lore is killed

implementationNotes:
OWED FROM THE #734 ROUND-4 REVIEW (reviewer verdict recorded verbatim on LCLI-797), carried here with the lifeline and the plugin installer's detached children.
F1, a pair-wide design gap routed to opum-doc by the leader: a nested quest native process can escape lore's sweep. lore spawns the npm quest.cjs wrapper with piped stdout and stderr, so quest.cjs finds no terminal and detaches its native child into its own session, outside lore's group; lore's kill(-lorepid, SIGKILL) reaches quest.cjs but not native quest. Deterministic where lore's sweep hits quest.cjs before it has forwarded (native lore killed by SIGKILL or OOM, and the exit-handler sweep after an uncaught exception); a race in the incident shape (SIGTERM to the wrapper reaches quest.cjs and native lore together, and the close-then-sweep can SIGKILL quest.cjs before its JS handler forwards, a window that widens under load). This contradicts DEC-282 (a2) item 1's grandchildren die with it, and the bin/lore.cjs docstring's 'A plain SIGTERM is fully handled'. Closed by quest's lifeline (QCLI-571). Until then CHANGELOG.md and the docstring should name it as a residual; the code was NOT changed for it, by the leader's instruction.
F5: test/bin-lore.test.ts SIGUSR1 witness is timing-dependent: dropping SIGUSR1 from NOT_RERAISED leaves the code and signal assertions unchanged, and only not.toContain('Debugger listening') catches it, which depends on the inspector printing before the loop drains and misses if port 9229 is busy. A deterministic witness would be a kills.cjs-style preload asserting no SIGUSR1 is sent to the wrapper's own pid.
F6: the SIGPIPE test passes against a mutant that drops SIGPIPE or SIGXFSZ from NOT_RERAISED, since Node ignores both; it guards behaviour and does not witness the change, and SIGXFSZ has no test. The exactly-once test is the real witness for N1.
F8: runLauncher does not pin stdin while startLauncher does; if Bun.spawnSync inherits a terminal stdin on a local run the exactly-once test takes the same-group branch and goes falsely red. Not a vacuous pass and not a CI concern.
F9: CHANGELOG.md, the 128+signal sentence sits inside the 'Also not covered' list as if it were an uncovered item.
